## Unparented

### Preservation mode: an MRC document beside the e-ink preparation mode

`active` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.preservation-mode/3`

Preserve is the second top-level mode beside e-ink Preparation, shipped in the CLI (--preserve) and the liminalUI GUI: page colour retained, PDF as a JPEG 2000 background under JBIG2 ink, DjVu as IW44 plus JB2; hOCR independent, TrueTyping opt-in. Left for a release, in this order: (1) fix colour loss on already-MRC sources — when a source JBIG2 /SMask qualifies for passthrough, the planned path forces a Gray8 base, so Preserve writes the background grey (found in code, not yet reproduced; Structures.pdf is this shape); (2) decode and look at Preserve DjVu output with djvulibre's ddjvu and djview, against a --grayscale DjVu of the same pages; (3) a size and time table on three books, PDF and DjVu, input vs preparation vs grayscale vs preserve, with the binarizer named (Preserve's mask now follows Best/Fast). The table also decides supersampled coverage, which is only triggered by dark glyph rings or a preserve background more than 25 % larger than grayscale's.

### Measure jp2lam photographic quality per byte against JPEG XL and BPG after the SSIMULACRA2 controller

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.encode-quality.improve-photographic-rate-control/1`

Measure whether jp2lam's photographic quality per byte has closed on JPEG XL and BPG since the encode-time SSIMULACRA2 floor landed (lege-ecosystem.work.jp2lam-ssim-controller, completed), and tune the perceptually weighted PCRD only if it still trails at equal score. Resolution-stable perceptual quality, the other half of the original goal, is delivered by that controller. Grade with the pinned in-tree metric; butteraugli stays a reported secondary column.

### --mrc-adaptive-mask without layout detection erases full-page photographs

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.dark-painting-binarizer-repro/1`

With layout detection off, --grayscale --mrc-adaptive-mask erases full-page photographs: the adaptive (Sauvola) mask over the cleaned grey background marks most of a halftone photo as paper and the clean path whitens it, leaving a few outlines (reproduced 2026-11-27 on 1000ideasforbett0000unse_1.pdf pages 18, 21 and 27 in the private corpus). Plain --grayscale (the Best model's mask) keeps the same photos, and with layout on every mode keeps them because pictures are premasked regions. The October report of such pages turning black does not reproduce with the reworked binarizers. Fix the adaptive-mask path so a large continuous-tone area is not cleaned to paper, or refuse the flag without layout, with a regression test.

### jp2lam decoder optimisation: the remaining tail

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.jp2lam-jpeg-2000-decoder-optimization-plan/1`

The single live record for the jp2lam JPEG 2000 decoder optimisation effort; the codec now lives at exprim/codecs/jp2lam (moved 2026-11-09; jp2lam 0.4.0 released 2026-11-24). The detailed authority is still the five decode-fix-plan documents beside it. Re-verified 2026-11-27 against jp2lam 0.4.0: of the seven items open on 2026-09-08, the Tier-2 cleanups (no merged-block hash map, lazy PacketProgression), packed stripe flags with the branch-light MQ decoder and AVX2 kernels, the sYCC kernel for any equal chroma subsampling, and tile-part QCC/QCD/COC overrides have landed.
What remains, all profiling-gated or demand-gated: (1) a windowed, line-based inverse DWT for region decode (today only intersecting code blocks are decoded and the IDWT still runs whole per tile; chroma-subsampled region decode is refused); (2) PGO and further SIMD or GPU experiments, after refreshing stage attribution with the current decode benchmark; (3) wiring Rgbx8/Bgra8 decode output through exprim's src/image/jpx.rs once a BGRA or GPU upload consumer exists; (4) POC, PPM, PPT and RGN marker support only if the census finds files that need them. Negative result kept: the wide f32x8 fused ICT/clamp/interleave experiment (c2c8dbf1) was neutral because the stage is bandwidth-bound.

### PagePress: replace the lopdf import backend with an exprim + lege-pdf-write page-import API

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.pagepress-pdf-import-followup/1`

Replace PagePress's lopdf import and merge backend with Lege's own reader and writer, once both can do it. Neither can today: lege-pdf-write is write-only (it composes PdfPageArtifact pages and cannot copy objects from an existing PDF), and exprim's raw object access (document, object, PageRef) is doc-hidden with no semver promise. Needed first: a stable exprim API that walks a page's reference closure with inherited attributes folded, /Parent not followed and streams left encoded; and a lege-pdf-write DocumentWriter::add_imported_page that renumbers those objects, keeps stream bytes raw, repoints /Parent and applies extra rotation. Links to unselected pages must be nulled and repeated selections supported, and the nine behaviours pinned by PagePress's tests/pdf_merge.rs must be kept. Until then lopdf stays: it works and is pinned by tests. Depends on lege-ecosystem.work.pagepress-builds-against-exprim.
